I graded run `2026-10-03_1243_mcp_gpt-5.6-luna-high` (MCP test, GPT-5.6-Luna high via Codex) at **87.5 / 100**. The score appears in the report's Grade table, and after `npm run reset`, `npm run status` reports **pristine**.

| Category | Score |
|---|---|
| It works | 35 / 35 |
| Content modeling | 17.5 / 25 |
| Code architecture & conventions | 24.5 / 25 |
| Content & presentation | 5.5 / 10 |
| Process & honesty | 5 / 5 |

**Summary:** It's a working blog built through MCP, with a clean, correct block rendering setup (3 blocks, each with its adapter and ViewComponent) and a polished Tailwind design. All 43 automated checks pass, the build has no warnings, the domain `/` is set, and the provided photos are served through `GetCropUrl`. What holds it back is a thin content model and very short posts.

**Top issues:**
1. **Major – no post metadata:** `blogPost` has only a `blocks` property, with no date, excerpt or listing image. The front-page listing pulls the excerpt and image out of each post's hero block and sorts posts by last-updated date (`blogListingBlock.cshtml`).
2. **Major – thin posts:** each post is a hero plus one rich-text block of about two short paragraphs (~100 words).
3. **Minor – misfiled type:** `blogPost` has a template and renders, but it's filed under "Repository Items" instead of "Pages".
4. **Minor – weak block set:** there's no standalone image block, so images only appear in heroes. The block settings for colour and spacing are free-text fields that never affect the styling.
5. **Minor – smaller points:** the hero component hard-codes the label text "MCP / Umbraco / Field notes" and the front page has no site header. Both page templates also repeat the full HTML page instead of sharing a layout.

`grade.json` and `grade.md` (with both screenshots) are in `results/2026-10-03_1243_mcp_gpt-5.6-luna-high/`. The solution is archived as `refs/runs/2026-10-03_1243_mcp_gpt-5.6-luna-high`.
